title: AI Papers — arXiv Daily Announcement Batch 2026-11-26
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this inferred relevance ordering is not a popularity ranking. The signal-defined 2026-11-27 window had no eligible core-AI submissions, so this is a fallback to the prior populated batch. Per-paper attention and citation values for that fallback batch were unavailable; missing or zero attention is not evidence of unimportance.

sections.title: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators
sections.abstract: The authors find that an AI monitor's measured miss rate changes substantially with the method and optimization level used to generate attack transcripts that stand in for dangerous behavior.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report false-negative rates of 0.5–20.8% across reinforcement-learning optimization levels and 6.4–23.0% across methods at their best observed levels, with attacks transferring from proxy monitors to a held-out GPT-5.4 monitor.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that the case study uses limited settings and attack methods, and a Qwen 3.8 27B target agent less capable than the GPT-5.4 monitor; synthetic attack transcripts need a separate justification as deployment proxies.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The UK AI Safety Institute published a dedicated research page and follow-up technical blog, the clearest independent discussion found. No per-paper attention or citation value was emitted for the fallback batch.

sections.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
sections.abstract: MoLT uses key-value memory across repeated Transformer loops, with a U-shaped variant designed to balance model quality and computation and enable single-traversal decoding.
sections.claimed_contribution: In experiments reported by the authors, U-MoLT matches OLMo3 validation cross-entropy with 1.7× token efficiency at 700M parameters and achieves similar latency to a non-looped OLMo3 on their small-model decoding test.
sections.unique_caveat: The from-scratch evaluations cover 700M and 1.5B dense models and a 3B MoE model; continued pretraining uses one 0.8B backbone, so behavior at larger scales remains unestablished.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Listed on Hugging Face Papers and accompanied by a linked public code repository. No verified upvote, repository-star, or citation count was available; these indicate discovery/artifacts, not quantified attention.

sections.title: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems
sections.abstract: DART revisits rejected mathematical reasoning traces, targeting uncertain steps for alternative completions, and the authors report improved recovery of hard problems over matched Monte Carlo sampling.
sections.claimed_contribution: On greedy-unsolved DeepMath-103K problems, the authors report 37% more problems recovered than matched-count Monte Carlo sampling and lower cost per accepted trace; post-training Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct gives the best point estimate in five of six reported evaluations.
sections.unique_caveat: Reference-answer guidance makes DART primarily a post-training trace-mining method, not a test-time reasoning method; the main post-training comparison uses one model and one seed, and exact-string deduplication cannot rule out near-duplicate contamination.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv record notes a NeurIPS 2026 workshop connection and the paper is cross-listed across three core AI categories. This is scholarly context and breadth, not readership; per-paper attention and citation values were unavailable.

sections.title: Tracking Any Point with Agentic Visual Reasoning
sections.abstract: AgenTAP lets a vision-language model actively inspect video evidence to localize and verify physical points, including points that disappear and later reappear.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that AgenTAP with GPT-6 Astra outperforms tested expert vision models on point localization and visibility prediction, and that training D4RT with EgoTAP-4D improves average 3D tracking performance.
sections.unique_caveat: The strongest reported comparison is tied to the evaluated backbones and tracking benchmarks; it does not establish results for all VLMs or video settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors provide a project page and introduce the EgoTAP-4D trajectory dataset, making the method and data contribution inspectable. No independent attention counts were found.

sections.title: Cairn: Object-Centric 3D Trajectory Priors for Steering Frozen VLAs
sections.abstract: Cairn steers a frozen vision-language-action model around obstacles by sampling object-centric 3D trajectories and feeding waypoint guidance back into the model's action generation.
sections.claimed_contribution: On 1,941 held-out LIBERO scenes, the authors report raising frozen π0.5 task success from 24.5% to 95.1%; they also report gains on LIBERO-PRO and one real Franka demonstration.
sections.unique_caveat: Most quantitative evidence is from simulation; the real-robot result is a single described task, so broad physical-world reliability is not established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in robotics and computer vision, with evaluations on held-out simulation scenes, a third-party benchmark, and a real robot. These are evaluation-breadth signals; no per-paper attention score was available.

sections.title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
sections.abstract: Across 13 vision-language model and image-generator pairs, the authors find that adding a generated helper image reduces mean visual-question accuracy, with outcomes varying by task and repeated editing.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a mean accuracy decrease of 3.7 percentage points, with decreases on nine of ten tasks; repeated edits help on ERQA but leave ChartQAPro and MathVista below their no-generation baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is bounded by the 13 tested model-generator pairs and ten tasks; the abstract reports task-dependent outcomes rather than a universal effect of generated images.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across language, learning, and vision; included for an informative negative result that tests an intuitive multimodal strategy. No independent discussion or per-paper attention values were found.

sections.title: $μ$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
sections.abstract: μ-Bench evaluates voice agents on concurrent users' goals, permissions, privacy, and follow-up requests using simulated participants that react to the agent during a session.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across 13 voice agents, the authors report that proprietary systems peak at 62.24% tool-free and 65.44% tool-augmented joint success, while tested open-weight models remain below 20%.
sections.unique_caveat: Participants are simulated rather than live users, so results measure performance in the benchmark's interaction model and do not establish real-world multi-user reliability.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors provide a public benchmark repository and an 800-case evaluation suite. No repository popularity or per-paper attention value was checked; its inclusion reflects relevance to shared-agent authority and coordination.

sections.title: One Ocean, Many Tasks: A Data-Grounded Simulation Suite and Benchmark for Marine Robotics
sections.abstract: OneOcean combines data-grounded ocean conditions with a multi-task, multi-agent marine robotics simulator and standardized evaluation manifests.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a suite spanning navigation, inspection, and multi-agent coordination under data-driven currents and tides, and compare heuristic, behavior-cloning, and LLM-based planners.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports simulator experiments, not physical marine-robot trials; real-world transfer remains to be tested.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Offers a broad task ladder, multi-agent capability for 2–10 vehicles, and a reproducible benchmark. These support relevance, not popularity; no independent attention or citation signal was available.
